title: Information Technology Ethics and Compliance, B.S. (College of Information Sciences and Technology)
notes: University Park. The entire IEC and ETI departments were missing -- added minimal entries in new iec_catalog.json/eti_catalog.json. Three real data gaps found and fixed: (1) 'MATH 22' requires MATH 21 (a real course, but never scheduled anywhere in this bulletin's own plan) -- substituted MATH 110 instead, matching the bulletin's own 'MATH 22 or higher' phrasing; (2) 'ETI 301'/'ETI 302' both require 'IST 210 and IST 220', but IST 220 is never scheduled in the bulletin's suggested plan at all -- added it as an explicit Semester 3 item alongside IST 210; (3) 'DS 435' requires 'DS 220', which itself requires CMPSC 121/131 -- neither CMPSC course appears anywhere in this bulletin's plan -- added CMPSC 131 (Semester 3) and DS 220 (Semester 4) as explicit prerequisite-chain items, same class of fix as Food Science's BMB 400 and CED's AEE 360 additions earlier this session. 'IST 495' (Internship, listed as a 1cr Summer course on the bulletin) is scheduled as a regular-term item since the engine paces by credit cap, not literal summer/fall/spring labels. The 12-credit 'Application Focus Area' pool (9 tracks: Business, Cybersecurity, Health Care, Human-Centered Design, Law & Policy, Organizational Leadership, ROTC, Security Risk Analysis, or Custom) is modeled generically, same convention as CMPSC's own open pools. Further real prereq-fix fallout: STAT 200 (Semester 3, its own item's other option DS 200 has the identical issue) now requires MATH 21, which itself requires MATH 4 and MATH 3 -- unlike the other majors in this batch, STAT 200 can't just be swapped for a no-prereq fallback here, since SRA 231 (Semester 4) has its own literal, unavoidable STAT 200 prereq (one of its two required AND-groups) -- so added MATH 3/MATH 4/MATH 21 as explicit Semester 1-3 items to genuinely unlock the chain; the engine's own scheduler pushes STAT 200 out to whichever later term MATH 21 actually completes in, which is fine at this major's 19cr/semester cap. STALENESS FIX (post 8caf0ae5, 'Add real PSU ALEKS math placement waivers; fix MATH 3/4 requirement bug'): MATH 3 and MATH 4 were added here as plan items to build a prereq chain into MATH 21 -- but that commit made planner_engine.expand_math_placement() unconditionally waive MATH 3 and MATH 4 for every student (their own catalog descriptions say they 'may not be used to satisfy the basic minimum requirements for graduation in any baccalaureate degree program'), and confirmed via the current catalog that MATH 21 itself has an EMPTY prereq_groups (its real prereq, 'MATH 4 or satisfactory performance on the mathematics placement examination', is a placement gate, not a literal course requirement -- same fact already verified for DATSC). So MATH 3 and MATH 4 were dead, unschedulable-for-a-real-reason plan items inflating this major's total credit count by 6 credits for no functional purpose -- removed both, kept MATH 21 (which is genuinely still required, per ACCTG 211/STAT 200's real prereq_groups). HANDBOOK VERIFICATION PASS (real bulletin PDF, bulletins.psu.edu/.../information-technology-ethics-compliance-bs/information-technology-ethics-compliance-bs.pdf): (1) the bulletin's own term-by-term suggested plan labels EVERY generic 'General Education Course' line as '(GN, GA, GH, or GHW)' -- a real, specific multi-domain restriction distinct from the university-wide Gen Ed pool, the same mechanism already used for CMPSC's combined-domain slots -- wired all 5 'GEN ED' slots with 'gen_ed': ['GN','GA','GH','GHW'] so they now actually recommend a real course instead of sitting as inert unlabeled placeholders. (2) The 'Application Focus Area' pool previously claimed to have '9 tracks' modeled generically -- the bulletin's own 'Application Focus Areas' section (further down the same page) enumerates the exact course list for 7 of those 9 tracks (Business Competency, Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations, Human-Centered Design and Development, Law & Policy, Organizational Leadership (WC), ROTC, Security Risk Analysis); wired all 4 'Application Focus Area' items with a 'match' regex built from that real list (the '(400-level)' item restricted to the 400+-numbered entries; ROTC modeled as AIR/ARMY/NAVSC department-prefix patterns rather than fabricated course numbers). 'Health Care' ('four courses from the HPA Minor or four courses from the Neuroscience Minor') has no enumerated course-by-course list on the bulletin and was intentionally left out rather than guessed. As with CMPSC's own curated elective lists, these remain unfilled recommendation placeholders and the 'must all come from one track' rule isn't enforced (deferred, not a bug).
